report.answer_text:
TikTok briefly went dark in the U.S. in January 2025, then stayed online while the Trump administration repeatedly delayed enforcement of a federal divest-or-ban law. ByteDance signed a deal in December, but the ownership change didn’t close until January 22, 2026. (apnews.com)
January–February: The Supreme Court upheld the law on January 17. TikTok went offline late January 18 and restored service on January 19 after Trump promised to delay enforcement. He signed the order on January 20, but TikTok didn’t return to Apple’s and Google’s U.S. app stores until February 13. (supremecourt.gov)
April–September: Trump extended the enforcement pause several times. On September 25, he signed an executive order approving a framework for a majority American-owned U.S. joint venture and giving the parties more time to close the deal. (govinfo.gov)
December and the closing: On December 18, TikTok told employees it had signed binding agreements with Oracle, Silver Lake, and MGX. When the deal closed in January 2026, those three investors each held 15% of TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC, and ByteDance retained 19.9%. (fidelity.com)
It wasn’t a sale of TikTok worldwide. The joint venture took responsibility for U.S. user data, recommendation-algorithm security, and content moderation, while U.S. users remained connected to the global platform. TikTok’s global business also kept certain commercial functions, including advertising and e-commerce. (newsroom.tiktok.com)

quotes.text: On April 4, 2025, I issued Executive Order 14258 (Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay), further delaying the Act's enforcement until June 19, 2025.
On June 19, 2025, I issued Executive Order 14310 (Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay), further delaying the Act's enforcement until September 17, 2025.
Finally, on September 16, 2025, I issued Executive Order 14350 (Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay), further delaying the Act's enforcement until December 16, 2025.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes show enforcement delays issued on April 4, June 19, and September 16, 2025, each further extending the TikTok enforcement pause, which backs the claim that the pause was extended several times between April and September 2025.

quotes.text: September 25, 2025 By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered
A plan has been presented to me to undergo a qualified divestiture of TikTok's United States operations, as outlined in a framework agreement (Framework Agreement).
It will be majority-owned and controlled by United States persons

Based on these findings, I further determine that the divestiture of the applications outlined in the Framework Agreement, once its implementation agreements are executed, is a "qualified divestiture" under the Act
To permit the contemplated divestiture to be completed, the Attorney General shall not take any action on behalf of the United States to enforce the Act for 120 days from the date of this order.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes back the September 25, 2025 order, the framework agreement, the majority U.S.-owned structure, and the 120-day enforcement delay, but none of them use the term "joint venture."
pages.page_reason: The September 25, 2025 order, signed by Donald J. Trump, determines that the proposed Framework Agreement qualifies for divestiture and describes a U.S.-based joint venture majority-owned and controlled by U.S. persons, while providing 120 days of non-enforcement to permit the divestiture to be completed.
